messages.subject: using linearComb for models with covariates, in order to backTransform
parts:
Hello all,

I get the feeling this is probably pretty easy and straight forward.  But, I’m new to unmarked, and fairly new to R as well.  I’m analysing occupancy (occupancy and detection probability) for introduced rats on islands in an archipelago in the tropical Pacific using ‘occu’.  I have two replicates of 100 samples each, collected at 50 sample stations on tourist visited islands and 50 on non-tourist visited islands.  My covariate (‘siteCovs’) is thus “tourist”.  All went smoothly until I tried to backTransform occupancy (‘state’ variable) in my model with the covariate (as I’d read would happen).  However, I’m not entirely sure how to use the linearComb feature to produce as “scalar linear combination” that I can then backTransform.  Here is what it looks like (please forgive the sloppiness - I copied and pasted from history in R Studio):


Call:
occu(formula = ~1 ~ Tourist, data = umf)

Occupancy:
            Estimate     SE     z P(>|z|)
(Intercept)    0.984  0.344 2.863 0.00419
Tourist        9.640 41.505 0.232 0.81633

Detection:
 Estimate    SE    z  P(>|z|)
     1.41 0.207 6.85 7.56e-12

AIC: 226.0303 
> backTransform(fm2['det'])
Backtransformed linear combination(s) of Detection estimate(s)

 Estimate     SE LinComb (Intercept)
    0.804 0.0325    1.41           1

Transformation: logistic 
> backTransform(fm2['state'])
Error in .local(obj, ...) : 
  Cannot directly back-transform an unmarkedEstimate with length > 1.
Use linearComb() and then backTransform() the resulting scalar linear combination.



I tried to take a stab at this, based on material I had read and seen online, but I'm not sure this is correct:


> lcfm2 <- linearComb(fm2, c(1,1), type='state')
> lcfm2
Linear combination(s) of Occupancy estimate(s)

 Estimate   SE (Intercept) Tourist
     10.6 41.5           1       1

> backTransform(lcfm2)
Backtransformed linear combination(s) of Occupancy estimate(s)

 Estimate      SE LinComb (Intercept) Tourist
        1 0.00101    10.6           1       1

Transformation: logistic


Am I close???  Thanks for any and all help, and your patience...


Paul Radley

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] using linearComb for models with covariates, in order to backTransform
parts:
Hi Paul,

I think I would ALWAYS just use the predict function for prediction. In your case, do something analogous to the following (hab is a factor with three levels):

# Fit model p(time+wind), psi(hab)

summary(fm2.occ <- occu(~time+wind-1 ~hab, data=umf))

 

# Predict occupancy for habitat factor levels

newdat <- data.frame(hab = c("A", "B", "C"))

predict(fm2.occ, type="state", newdata = newdat, appendData = TRUE)


This gives this:
  Predicted         SE      lower     upper hab
1 0.1139666 0.07914607 0.02693418 0.3741059   A
2 0.6579139 0.15598369 0.33084338 0.8820925   B
3 0.7100853 0.13388848 0.40639000 0.8975695   C

Which is what you want.

Best regards  --- Marc

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] using linearComb for models with covariates, in order to backTransform
parts:
Thanks so much for the reply, Marc...

And that's good to hear, I'm headed in the correct direction.  Last night, well after I posted here, I came upon an overview of unmarked written by Fiske and Chandler and dated 14 May 2017.  I redid my analysis following that and it seems like it came out the way it should.  And your input here further confirms that.  The results look like this:


> newData <- data.frame(Tourist=0:1)
> round(predict(fm2, type='det', newdata=newData, appendData=TRUE), 2)
  Predicted   SE lower upper Tourist
1      0.52 0.05  0.41  0.62       0
2      0.89 0.03  0.80  0.94       1
> predict(fms, type='det', newdata=newData)
  Predicted         SE     lower     upper
1 0.5191853 0.05424816 0.4135946 0.6230897
2 0.8896665 0.03414701 0.8030614 0.9409851


And thanks again.  I'll have another question to post, about another data set, in the not too distant future...

Cheers,
Paul
